key_insight: Real patient-chatbot conversations are much more diverse than idealised simulations, and that diversity can change how LLMs judge urgency.
clinical_relevance: Symptom-checking chatbots should be built and tested to handle different emotional states, communication styles, and conversational strategies to avoid biased or unsafe triage performance.
method: Built a patient simulator that models clinical content, emotion, strategy, and communication style separately
Evaluated urgency assessment across five patient personae in 1,164 clinician-graded cases with four LLMs
evidence_signal: In a Turing-inspired realism test, 15 human graders identified simulated conversations with only 55% accuracy, suggesting the simulator was close to real patient dialogue.
watch_item: Results come from simulated and retrospective evaluations, so real-world deployment still needs careful monitoring because communication style alone may shift triage outcomes.
paper_title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
